android.desc: Your Japanese IC card companion Suikakeibo is your Japanese IC card companion for quick balance checks, transaction history and expense tracking. Add notes to your purchases, keep multiple cards organized, and export selected trips to CSV for expense reports. MAIN FEATURES • Balance checks: scan a supported Japanese IC card to see its balance. Never get the buzzer at the gate again. • Saved history: scan recent transactions from your card and keep them saved in the app • Trip details: see fares, with station names in Japanese or English • Spending summaries: review transport and shopping expenses by month and category • Notes: record what a purchase was for • CSV export: select records to help prepare travel expense reports • Multiple cards: keep balances and history for all your cards organized in one app • Home-screen widgets: see your last scanned balance at a glance • Customizable card colors, backgrounds and designs. Dark/Light mode supported FREE VERSION AND PREMIUM The free version limits how many history records you can view and export to CSV. Premium removes these limits and unlocks advanced statistics and custom card backgrounds. See the app for features and pricing. SUPPORTED CARDS Suica, PASMO, ICOCA, Kitaca, TOICA, manaca, SUGOCA, nimoca, hayakaken, SAPICA, icsca, IruCa and more. E-money cards including WAON, nanaco and Rakuten Edy can also be scanned. Available information varies by card and transaction type. HOW SCANNING WORKS Scanning with your phone requires an NFC-enabled device. Hold the card against your phone's reading area for a few seconds. Balances and history reflect your last scan. Scan again to update them, including the balance shown in your widget. Cards hold a limited number of recent records. Scan regularly before older records are overwritten; the app cannot recover records already overwritten on the card. Scanned records are saved in the app and can be viewed within your plan's history limit. Journeys that are not recorded on the card, such as travel covered by a commuter pass, cannot be displayed. This app cannot top up your IC cards. SUPPORT Help and FAQs: https://suikakeibo.jp/en/faq Contact: help@mediavrog.net

> The only thing I didn't like about Suica/Pasmo when I was in Japan was that, unlike a credit card, there doesn't seem to be a way to get a statement so you can see where you spent all your money

I use Suikakeibo [0] for that. The latest 20-ish transactions seem to be stored on the card, so by scanning it using my phone every day I could keep a history of everything I used it for. You can even put in notes, since non-transit transaction don't list what you bought with it - just the amount.

It makes for a nice reminder of my past trips. =)

[0] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.mediavrog.ic_card_expensetracker
